report.summary: Visible concurrency flaw in _init_db can cause 'database is locked' when multiple processes initialise. Docstring claims record_journal_watermark enforces append-only journal position but this method is absent from the visible slice. _embed_batch swallows errors silently. Zero-vector rejected even for 'none' normalisation (debatable).
risks: CONCURRENCY: _init_db migration runs in a transaction without retry; parallel first opens on the same DB (common in WSGI/async workers) will hit SQLITE_BUSY and crash the process. Windows file locking makes this worse.
DOCSTRING MISMATCH: docstring promises record_journal_watermark enforces monotonic watermarks and hash consistency, but no such method is visible in this file.
ERROR SWALLOWING: _embed_batch catches EmbeddingError and returns None silently. Callers may treat None as success, leading to missing vectors.

POTENTIAL CORRECTNESS: _normalize_vector rejects zero norm even when normalisation='none', which may be unexpected if callers want to store zero vectors (but docstring justifies it for cosine safety).
MISSING IMPLEMENTATION: Search/ingest methods (search_report, ingest_report) are referenced in docstring but not visible; their actual enforcement cannot be verified.
todos: Add retry logic or WAL mode + busy timeout to handle concurrent _init_db safely.
Confirm whether record_journal_watermark is defined; if not, remove docstring promise or implement it.
Consider logging or a more explicit return type in _embed_batch to prevent silent failures.
Review zero-vector policy for 'none' normalisation to see if it should be allowed for pure storage use cases.

handoff.suggestion: Focus on concurrency hardening of _init_db (e.g., setting PRAGMA busy_timeout before migration, or opening with URI file:?mode=rwc&nolock=1 as last resort). Also verify that record_journal_watermark exists elsewhere; if not, update the docstring to avoid false promises.
